biography: Josh Steed, a name now synonymous with aggressive Ginetta racing, hails from a small town in rural England where the only form of motorsport was the annual lawnmower race. His father, a mechanic, instilled in him a love for engines and the thrill of competition. Josh's racing career began relatively late, at age 21, after he scraped together enough money to buy a used Ginetta G40. His natural talent was immediately apparent, dominating local club races. A defining moment came at Brands Hatch in 2015; starting last after a qualifying mishap, Steed carved his way through the field, executing daring overtakes, ultimately finishing second. This performance caught the eye of a small Ginetta team, marking his entry into professional racing. Now, at 33, Steed is considered to be in his prime, battling for podiums and championships, a relentless force on the track. He is known for his absolute commitment to racing, with rumors that he still sleeps in the garage during race weekends to remain close to his car.
drivingStyle: Steed's driving style is best described as 'controlled aggression.' He's known for late braking and daring overtakes, often pushing the limits of grip. He attacks corners with a ferocity that unnerves his rivals, willing to risk it all for a position. While his tire management isn't always the most refined, he compensates with pure speed and an uncanny ability to anticipate changes in track conditions. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest.

careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Spa in 2021 due to a mechanical failure, ending his team's hopes of victory and leaving him visibly devastated.
